full_judgment: 8. Before we part with the record we feel it necessary to observe that we have purposely refrained from making any observation on the merit of the allegations against the petitioner although Mr. Mujibur Rahman sought to argue that there was hardly any case against the petitioner to go for trial. We have only examined the impugned orders in the light of the legal provisions and come to the conclusion as aforesaid. It may be that the informant father of the deceased has a genuine grievance against the police investigation and the dismissal of the petition of complaint by the Sub-Divisional Magistrate, it may be that the facts and Circumstances of the case deserve that there should be a further inquiry in so far as the petitioner is concerned. There is no limitation as regard criminal process and if so advised the informant may yet pursue his remedy in accordance with law.
